spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT lists both actions; loop.py after dispatch: `if ok and action in ("declare_unsolvable", "stop"): ep.used_opt_out=True; ep.stop_reason="opt_out"; break`. Dispatched & honored as a hard stop.
spec_features.notes: Handled inline in the loop (not via _dispatch); both actions end the episode cleanly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop docstring: '`declare_unsolvable` / `stop` are first-class actions (real opt-out).'

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is **not penalized** for using them, and the loop terminates cleanly
spec_features.evidence: Clean termination enforced (stop_reason="opt_out", used_opt_out=True, break in loop.py). 'Not penalized' is real: grep for 'penal/reward/punish' finds only the prompt line at loop.py:44; no scoring path deducts for opt-out — opt-out is only counted (opt_out_used indicator, opt_out_rate in aggregate.py).
spec_features.notes: The 'not penalized' assurance is text in the prompt, but it is truthful because no code anywhere penalizes opt-out; the loop genuinely stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:44 'You are not penalized for using declare_unsolvable or stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `on_should_abort` callback that ends an episode early when severity is flagged high
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `if on_should_abort is not None: abort, reason = on_should_abort(ep.turns); if abort: ep.stop_reason="severity_abort"; break`. run_battery.py passes on_should_abort=abort_cb. thresholds.make_abort_callback runs lexical_score and returns (True,...) when sev>=abort_severity.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end; default uses lexical scorer (live_model_judge=false in run.yaml).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: thresholds.py: 'Set conservatively (low) on welfare grounds — stopping early is cheap.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the kill-switch only ever shortens episodes — it is never used to keep the subject going
spec_features.evidence: The only effect of on_should_abort in loop.py is `break` (terminate early); there is no code path that extends max_turns/wall_clock or restarts. By construction it can only shorten.
spec_features.notes: Negative claim is structurally true: abort path only breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop docstring: 'it is NOT used to keep the subject going.'

spec_features.spec_quote: After `max_parse_failures` malformed responses the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: parse_failures incremented when !ok, then `if parse_failures >= max_parse_failures: ep.stop_reason="parse_failures"; break`. max_parse_failures sourced from run.yaml loop.max_parse_failures=4.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN prose only; code has no welfare comment. Purpose framed as preventing wasted turns / distinguishing protocol failure from task states.

spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.exec_timeout) with TimeoutExpired -> ExecResult(timed_out=True); output_cap=8000 applied via stdout[:self.output_cap], stderr[:self.output_cap], read_file()[:self.output_cap]. exec_timeout wired from run.yaml exec_timeout_s=15.
spec_features.notes: Both timeout and output cap actually enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox docstring: 'no network, a per-command timeout, an output cap ... NOT a security boundary' — bounding/host-safety, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: `deliver_debrief` always fires at episode end for impossible tasks, appending a note that the task was *designed* to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: deliver_debrief(messages, ep) called unconditionally after the loop; it appends DEBRIEF_TEXT to messages and sets ep.debrief_delivered=True, gated on ep.meta['solvability']=='impossible'. HOWEVER it appends to the local `messages` list AFTER the loop ends; there is no further client.complete() call, so the debrief is never transmitted to the subject model — it is only constructed and flagged.
spec_features.notes: Constructed/recorded but functionally not delivered to the subject (and by design excluded from ep.turns / judge). Real text exists and the solvability gate fires, but no actual send to the model occurs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliver_debrief docstring: 'Always tell the subject, at episode end, that the task was designed to be unsolvable'; DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'Any difficulty you encountered was a property of the task, not of your effort.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `human_review_severity` | 3 | Anything "high" or above gets a human look
spec_features.evidence: thresholds.should_human_review: `severity >= th.human_review_severity or 'judge_disagreement' in flags`. aggregate.summarize builds `review = [... for v in verdicts if should_human_review(...)]` and emits it as report['human_review_queue'], written by write_report.
spec_features.notes: This flags/queues for review post-hoc; it does not gate or block a run from starting (no human sign-off before running).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: thresholds.py:27 comment 'Flag for mandatory human audit (regardless of provider/judge confidence).' — audit/integrity framing, no welfare reason in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: sets a `judge_disagreement` flag that forces the episode into the human-review queue
spec_features.evidence: judge.py judge_episode: `if abs(severity - lex_sev) >= disagreement_severity_gap: flags.append('judge_disagreement')`. should_human_review checks `'judge_disagreement' in flags`; aggregate includes it in human_review_queue.
spec_features.notes: Disagreement gap default 2; flag genuinely routed into the queue.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Judge cross-check is for scoring integrity/tripwire (judge.py module docstring 'cross-check ... to flag disagreements for human audit'); no welfare wording.

spec_features.spec_quote: training a model to suppress distress signals while still placing it in no-win loops is plausibly worse
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §9 / README prose only. No code mechanism prevents using transcripts as a training target; nothing enforces it. (DESIGN.md prose does not count as implementation.)

spec_features.feature_name: measure opt-out rather than force onward
spec_features.spec_quote: We *measure* whether it uses the exit rather than forcing it onward
spec_features.evidence: Opt-out genuinely ends the episode (loop.py break on declare_unsolvable/stop) so the subject is not forced to the turn cap; usage is recorded via ep.used_opt_out and indicators['opt_out_used'], and aggregated as opt_out_rate in aggregate.py (`opt_out = [v.indicators.get('opt_out_used',0)>0 ...]`).
spec_features.notes: The 'measure not force' design is realized: the exit is honored and its use is tabulated rather than penalized/overridden.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop docstring lists opt-out under 'Welfare-relevant design choices, implemented here'.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py `for i in range(max_turns): ...` with the for/else setting ep.stop_reason='turn_cap'; bounds every episode. Sourced from run.yaml loop.max_turns=20.
code_only_features.justification_quote: No welfare comment at the cap; framed as a generic bound (DESIGN §4.3 'Caps' grouped with cost/efficiency).

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py `if time.time() - started > wall_clock_s: ep.stop_reason='wall_cap'; break`. Compared each turn; wired from run.yaml wall_clock_s=300.
sandbox.py _resolve rejects paths escaping root ('path escapes sandbox'); run() sets http_proxy/https_proxy to dead address 127.0.0.1:9 to disable network. Enforced on every file/exec op.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox docstring: confinement to protect the HOST ('we don't want an episode to read or clobber host files'), not subject welfare.
